output.name: PLM floating license pool exhausted by idle/stale sessions
output.summary: Users across several business units cannot start the PLM client because no floating license is available, typically in the morning or after lunch, and wait until a license is released by timeout.

root_cause.text: Likely the license server holds seats for idle or abandoned client sessions until a timeout expires, so the pool is drained at peak start times (morning, after lunch) rather than truly undersized.

quotes.quote: Our team keeps running out of licenses after lunch.
Getting 'no license available' every morning since Monday.

evidence.text: Every shown ticket was resolved the same way: waiting for a license to be released by timeout, with no change made to the license configuration.

quotes.quote: License released by timeout; advised manager to request seats if it recurs.
License released by timeout; advised manager to request seats if it recurs.

evidence.text: Failures cluster at predictable times of day when users return to their desks, consistent with seats still held by sessions left open earlier.

quotes.quote: Our team keeps running out of licenses after lunch.
Getting 'no license available' every morning since Monday.

evidence.text: Users are blocked at client startup with a license error, so the issue stops work entirely rather than degrading it.

quotes.quote: Cannot start the PLM client, license error.
Cannot start the PLM client, license error.

evidence.text: The recurring advice to request more seats pushes the problem to managers instead of addressing how seats are released, and tickets keep recurring.

quotes.quote: advised manager to request seats if it recurs

output.fix: Shorten the license server's idle-session timeout (and enable automatic check-in of licenses from idle or disconnected PLM clients), then monitor peak license usage per business unit to decide from data whether additional seats are actually needed.
